  <div class="main">
    <section class="home-section" id="about" aria-labelledby="about-title">
      <h2 class="section__title" id="about-title">About</h2>
      <p>I study the dynamics of physical systems and develop learning methods for their control and optimization. My work connects models of evolving physical states with decisions about system operation and manufacturing conditions. I am particularly interested in neural operators for distributed dynamics and in how model errors affect the resulting decisions.</p>
      <p>My engineering interests lie in water-energy systems, with a current emphasis on the dynamics and sustainable operation of integrated multi-energy systems serving data centers. I am interested in how computing demand interacts with cooling and energy supply, and how these interactions affect energy and water use alongside carbon emissions.</p>
      <p>My scientific work focuses on dynamic modeling and optimization for precision materials manufacturing. I work with <a href="https://www.peese.org/professor/">Professor Fengqi You</a> to model how material structure evolves during processing and to optimize processing conditions for desired structures.</p>
      <p>I am an Ezra Systems Postdoctoral Associate in Systems Engineering at Cornell University. I completed my Ph.D. at Shanghai Jiao Tong University in 2026, advised by <a href="https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/author/37280547200">Professor Jingcheng Wang</a>.</p>
    </section>

    <section class="home-section" id="research" aria-labelledby="research-title">

          <h3 class="note__title"><a href="/thinking/#what-status-buys">What status buys</a></h3>
          <p>We chase money and status largely for the life they can buy. If AI expands supply and makes that life affordable to more people, climbing the hierarchy becomes less necessary and following an interest becomes easier. If the bubble bursts without delivering those gains, why panic about missing a revolution that never arrived?</p>
        </article>
